blocks.title: Pappus's hexagon theorem: the three cross intersections are collinear, and ONE non-degeneracy condition suffices

summary.text: the saturated cofactor certificate over a SINGLE non-degeneracy condition, re-checked from the committed artifact by a checker that shares no code with either of the two searches that produced it

caption.text: Evidence row geometry-certificate-pappus-hexagon as recorded in the ledger

rows: geometry_check::check_certificate shape pass (the saturation generator is REBUILT here as `parallel(A,E,B,D) * Zinv0 - 1` from the condition polynomial the file declares, and compared with the generator the cofactors are taken against; the eight hypothesis generators are compared against the stated hypotheses unchanged, which is what stops a solved-form substitution from being passed off as a proof of the original statement), geometry_check::check_certificate symbolic pass (the identity target = sum of cofactor times generator expanded with MvPoly add/mul alone -- no Groebner machinery, no monomial order, no S-polynomials, and no linear algebra either; 74 cofactor terms over 9 generators), geometry_check::check_certificate numeric pass (the same identity re-evaluated at 24 deterministic integer points through MvPoly::evaluate, a different code path from the symbolic expansion), geometry_check::check_certificate usage pass (the saturation generator must carry a NONZERO cofactor, or the certificate would be advertising a weaker theorem than it proved), geometry_check::check_certificate degenerate-witness pass (A=(0,0), B=(1,0), C=(3,0), D=(1,0), E=(0,0), F=(5,0), X=(0,1), Y=(2,0), Z=(4,0) replayed: all eight hypotheses vanish, the condition polynomial vanishes, and the conclusion does NOT), geometry_check::check_certificate configuration pass (A=(0,0), B=(1,0), C=(3,0) on the x-axis with D=(0,2), E=(2,3), F=(4,4) on a second line and X=(4/7,6/7), Y=(6/5,6/5), Z=(31/13,24/13) replayed: hypotheses vanish, the condition does not, the conclusion does)
the saturated cofactor certificate over a SINGLE non-degeneracy condition, re-checked from the committed artifact by a checker that shares no code with either of the two searches that produced it

certified 2026-08-15 in 6.7 ms, checker-verified, with condition set ["ae-meets-bd"]. One 2x2 block is eliminated by adjugate (determinant exactly the condition polynomial), leaving a 48-term degree-4 residue over the six untouched hypotheses; `cofactor_ansatz` settles that residue at cofactor degree 2 in about 25 ms with every coefficient +-1. The same residue was handed to the cofactor-tracked Buchberger route on an idle host and was killed after 7.5 minutes without returning, which is why the bounded-degree linear-algebra route is tried first. For contrast with the previous state of this...

kind.text: The certificate uses the Rabinowitsch trick: a fresh variable Zinv0 and the generator `parallel(A,E,B,D) * Zinv0 - 1`. Specialising Zinv0 := 1/det(E-A, D-B) is legitimate exactly when AE is not parallel to BD, and that is the ONLY place the side condition enters. The multiplier is the condition polynomial to the FIRST power, so the saturation cofactor is the familiar minus-the-conclusion rather than euler-line's squared-multiplier shape. Every tamper control in the cited suite runs against this certificate too: a cofactor edited by one is rejected, a conclusion edited by one is rejected, a swapped non-degeneracy condition is rejected, cofactors donated by a neighbouring certificate are rejected, deleting the degenerate counterexample is rejected, and replacing it with the on-locus-but-harmless configuration (the same six collinear points with X=(0,0) instead of (0,1), which violates the condition just as thoroughly and yet leaves X, Y, Z collinear) is rejected.

summary.text: that the single non-degeneracy condition this certificate consumes is minimal ABSOLUTELY rather than budget-relative (ADR-0455)

caption.text: Evidence row geometry-condition-minimality-pappus-hexagon as recorded in the ledger

rows: `every_used_condition_set_is_minimal_absolutely` replays, for every PROPER subset S of the conditions a committed certificate uses, a configuration that satisfies every hypothesis, keeps every condition in S nonzero, and FALSIFIES a conclusion -- which refutes membership in the saturated ideal of S outright, since a member would have to vanish at every common zero of those generators, the same configuration is independently replayed by geometry_check::check_certificate's degenerate-witness pass, from the artifact, by code that knows nothing about minimality, `a_counterexample_on_the_locus_that_falsifies_nothing_is_rejected` confirms the counterexample is doing more than sitting on the degeneracy locus, and asserts full coverage of every certificate's coordinatisation so this theorem cannot silently opt out of that control

1 proper subset of 1 condition refuted for this fact; 5 proper subsets across the 5 saturated certificates in the corpus (each uses exactly one condition, so each has exactly one proper subset -- the empty one), 0 undecided.

kind.text: The only proper subset of a one-element condition set is the empty one, and the six-collinear-points configuration satisfies all eight hypotheses while falsifying the conclusion -- so the conclusion is not in the plain hypothesis ideal, decided, with no budget, no monomial order and no algorithm anywhere in the argument. This is the second geometry fact whose minimality is established this way rather than by the 2^n subset audit `geometry_order_audit` runs, and on this theorem the audit is not an option: the Groebner route does not return here at all.

summary.text: that the two conditions this theorem states and does NOT use are individually redundant -- so the three-element set previously reported for it was not merely unproved-minimal but genuinely non-minimal

caption.text: Evidence row geometry-condition-redundancy-pappus-hexagon as recorded in the ledger

rows: `each_pappus_condition_alone_certifies` restricts the problem to one stated condition at a time -- so the subset search has no other option -- and requires a CERTIFICATE for each of the three, re-expanding the identity against the original generators. All three certify at cofactor degree 2. That is a statement about Q, not about a sample: a certificate is a polynomial identity, `pappus_condition_subsets` decides the question exhaustively over F_p by enumerating every carrier-line pair up to the affine group and every solution of the six incidence hypotheses, INCLUDING the positive-dimensional solution sets where a cross point is under-determined, which is exactly where the question bites. It reads the hypothesis, condition and conclusion polynomials out of the committed corpus and reduces them mod p term by term, so it cannot agree with a formula the corpus does not hold, the affine-orbit reduction that makes the larger primes reachable is itself checked: `--full` enumerates every first carrier triple and agrees with the orbit run at p = 5 (5,580,000 configurations with all three conditions nonzero, and the same single refuting pattern)

that the two conditions this theorem states and does NOT use are individually redundant -- so the three-element set previously reported for it was not merely unproved-minimal but genuinely non-minimal

3 of 3 stated conditions certify alone (52, 52 and 56 cofactor terms, all at cofactor degree 2). Exhaustive over F_p for p = 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23: of the 8 zero/nonzero patterns of the three conditions, exactly 1 admits a refuting configuration -- the all-zero pattern -- so every singleton and every pair is unrefutable and the empty set is refuted. Cross-checked at p = 5 against a full (non-orbit) enumeration, and the count of configurations with all three conditions nonzero (10,680 orbit-reduced at p=5; 5,580,000 full at p=5; 96,600 at p=7; 1,631,520 at p=11; 4,547,400 at p=13) was ind...

kind.text: This row exists because the previous lane's reading of the same evidence was the opposite one. Three attempts to find a configuration isolating a single condition had collapsed, always because killing one intersection forced the two other constructed points onto the very line the freed point was confined to, and that was recorded as an obstruction to claiming minimality. It is not: it is the reason each condition is redundant. The incidence hypotheses assert that X, Y and Z EXIST on their line pairs, so a configuration where one line pair degenerates does not lose that point, it frees it along a line -- and every way that can happen drags the other two cross points onto that same line. The distinction matters for the ledger because the two readings differ in what they license: 'we could not decide the subsets' invites a budget-relative fact, while 'a smaller subset provably suffices' means the larger set must not be filed at all.

rows: lane pappus-minimality: axeyum_cas::linear_elim (adjugate elimination of the single licensed 2x2 block) + axeyum_cas::cofactor_ansatz (bounded-degree ideal membership by exact sparse linear algebra, which settles the residue Buchberger does not return on) + axeyum_cas::geometry_certify::certify_by_linear_elimination with licensed_blocks (the condition subset chooses the decomposition, not the other way round) + axeyum_cas::geometry_check (independent re-derivation)

classical; coordinatised and certified with three conditions by the `euler-linearity` lane, which held it off the ledger because it could not establish minimality, and completed by the `pappus-minimality` lane, which found that the three-condition set was not minimal at all

caption.text: Prior art recorded in the ledger

rows: standard historical attribution; this lane did not consult the primary source
if A, B, C lie on one line and D, E, F on another, the three cross intersections AE.BD, AF.CD and BF.CE are collinear
Synagoge (Mathematical Collection), Book VII, propositions 138-139, c. 340 CE

kind.text: Established on the `cas-certificate` route, in the geometry family. What this fact records that is new is not the theorem -- Pappus is c. 340 CE -- but a failure mode in how a mechanised proof reports its own hypotheses. A search that returns 'the smallest condition subset that succeeded' is reporting a property of ITS OWN decomposition unless something forces the two to agree. Here the block detector always found all three intersection blocks, so the multiplier was always the product of all three conditions, so every proper subset failed at the multiplier-division step for a reason that had nothing to do with the theorem -- and the honest-looking output was a three-condition theorem that is false as a minimality claim. `licensed_blocks` closes it by making the condition subset choose the decomposition rather than inherit it: a block may be eliminated only if its determinant is a nonzero rational times a product of powers of the conditions currently being inverted. That is a soundness-shaped rule doing an honesty-shaped job, and it took 292 s and three conditions down to 6.7 ms and one. `geometry.nondegeneracy.ae-meets-bd` is listed in the axiom footprint even though it also appears as a hypothesis of `formal.statement`, deliberately: the footprint is the field a reader scans to see what a proof rests on, and a side condition invisible there is precisely how a mechanised geometry proof comes to be quoted as unconditional. The SMT-LIB transcription above was cross-evaluated against the certificate's own polynomials at 400 random rational configurations, 4000 comparisons, zero mismatches, using a checker first validated by reproducing F:geometry-euler-line's own claim of 2400 comparisons and zero mismatches.
